description: The line plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for various models, including a baseline "Vanilla" model and several variants of the SepLLM approach with different configurations. The x-axis, labeled "#Iteration," represents the number of training iterations, ranging from 0 to 140,000 on a linear scale, with major tick marks at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis, labeled "Loss," shows the model's loss value, ranging from 2.4 to 3.4 on a linear scale, with major tick marks at intervals of 0.1. All lines begin at a high loss value near 3.3 at iteration 0 and exhibit a steep initial decline. The "Vanilla" model (purple line) shows a consistent decrease in loss, stabilizing around 2.5 by the end of the training. The "StrmLLM (n=64)" model (blue line) follows a similar trajectory, with a slightly lower loss than Vanilla after the initial drop. The "SepLLM (n=64)" model (orange line) and the "SepLLM (n=64, H)" model (green line) both show a very similar trend, with the green line slightly below the orange line, indicating a marginally better performance. The "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" model (red line) follows a trajectory very close to the "SepLLM (n=64)" model. Finally, the "SepLLM (n=128)" model (dark blue line) shows a distinct trend, starting with a higher loss than the other models but then decreasing rapidly and stabilizing at a loss value slightly above 2.5, indicating that increasing the number of separators from 64 to 128 leads to a different convergence behavior.
